Action Plan:
1. Acute wheeze/shortness of breath (suspected asthma exacerbation):
   - Use salbutamol inhaler 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially.
   - Spacer prescribed; pharmacist to demonstrate correct technique.
   - Peak flow meter prescribed; record peak flow twice daily (on waking and in the evening) for 1 week.
   - Safety-net: call clinic promptly if temperature becomes high or wheezing/shortness of breath worsens.
   - Arrange asthma review in ~1 week (earlier if deterioration) to discuss results and consider additional controller therapy.
2. Allergic rhinitis:
   - Start a regular over-the-counter antihistamine (agent/dose not documented); pharmacy advice to be noted in chart.

Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Reason for visit: Wheeze and shortness of breath for 2–3 days.
- HPI:
  - Symptoms: Wheeze, dyspnea on walking, reduced exercise tolerance; occasional difficulty completing sentences over the last few days; daytime cough; no chest pain; no sputum; no hemoptysis; not waking at night; currently feels well at rest; can manage stairs.
  - Temperature: Patient reported “fever,” then reported measured 37°C (conflict noted).
  - No peak flow meter at home; has an inhaler; no spacer.
- Past medical history:
  - Asthma in childhood (reportedly “quite bad”); occasional hospital visits (no ICU).
  - Hay fever; eczema.
  - States asthma “stopped” 3–4 years ago (conflict with current use of salbutamol noted).
- Medications:
  - Salbutamol inhaler used “normally,” approximately every few weeks and with exercise (dose/route/frequency not documented beyond plan).
  - No other regular meds.
- Allergies:
  - No known drug allergies.
- Social history:
  - Non-smoker.
  - Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine every 2–3 days.
  - Lives with partner.
  - Occupation: Engineer; currently working from home/occasional sick leave due to symptoms.

Objective:
- Examination: Not performed (telehealth).
- Patient-reported data:
  - Temperature measured at home: 37°C (patient also reported “fever”; conflict noted).
  - Functional status: Not breathless at rest; short of breath with walking; can climb stairs.
- Investigations: None performed today.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute wheeze/shortness of breath (suspected asthma exacerbation):
   - Assessment: Acute asthma exacerbation.
   - Differential diagnosis: Viral respiratory infection; allergen exposure (pollen) as triggers.
   - Investigations planned: Home peak flow monitoring twice daily for 1 week.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Salbutamol inhaler 2–4 puffs every 4 hours initially via spacer.
     - Spacer prescribed; pharmacist to instruct on use.
   - Relevant referrals: None.
   - Follow-up: Asthma review in ~1 week to assess control, review peak flow diary, and consider controller therapy; earlier review if worsening.

2. Allergic rhinitis (hay fever):
   - Assessment: Allergic rhinitis contributing as a potential trigger.
   - Treatment planned: Begin regular OTC antihistamine (agent/dose/frequency not documented); pharmacist to advise per note.
   - Relevant referrals: None.
   - Follow-up: As above with asthma review.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements:
  - Full vitals (HR, RR, SpO2, BP), in-person respiratory exam.
  - Detailed medication reconciliation (specific inhaler brand/dose, frequency).
  - Inhaler technique assessment (to be done with spacer pickup).
  - Personalized written asthma action plan.
  - Peak flow predicted values not documented.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Fever: Patient reported “fever,” but also reported temperature 37°C (normal) — conflict noted.
  - Asthma history/medication: Patient stated asthma stopped 3–4 years ago and not taking medication, yet also reports “normally” using salbutamol every few weeks and with exercise — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; occasional hesitations and brief communication gaps.
